result.title: UCB-min: Combining Bandits Under Variance Heterogeneity (Extended Version)
result.comment: Extended version of short conference paper accepted at IEEE BigData 2026
result.summary: Multi-armed bandits are a natural framework for many real-world sequential decision problems, from recommender systems and clinical trials to educational test recommendation and online advertising. The performance of these algorithms depends on how they explore different arms, and exploration strategies range from variance-independent (e.g., UCB1) to variance-aware (e.g., UCB-V). In practice the reward variance of each arm is rarely known and varies widely across arms, and the reward support is often underspecified. In these cases no single rule is uniformly best: variance-independent methods are robust but loose when variances are small, while variance-aware methods are tight only when their variance estimates and the assumed support bound are reliable. Such heterogeneous, unknown variances arise in many settings, for instance when multiple objectives are scalarized into a single reward. We propose UCB-min, a per-arm adaptive meta-algorithm that selects, for each arm, the tighter of a variance-independent and a variance-aware exploration bonus, without prior knowledge of the variance regime and without reward normalization. We prove that, with UCB-V as variance-aware base, its regret is bounded by the sum of the two base bounds at the standard exploration constant, and by their per-arm minimum, up to a constant, for a larger one. We validate it on synthetic data, an educational tutoring task, and two group-recommendation benchmarks (MovieLens, Steam), showing that UCB-min consistently tracks the best base algorithm across diverse variance regimes and datasets.

AI.brief_summary: 论文提出 UCB-min：在方差异质且未知的情形下，为每个臂自适应地在方差无关与方差感知两类探索奖励中选取更紧的一项，并给出 regret 上界，用合成数据、教育推荐和两个群组推荐基准验证。
AI.relevance_reason: 其「按单元在稳健与高效估计之间自适应切换、并以 regret 刻画代价」的思路，可能为 LVR 中逐步选择计算/证据获取方式与停止决策提供可核查的线索，但需判断多臂设定能否对应推理中的状态与成本结构。
